body:
Closing as superseded — Kaushalt2004's PR #141 (merge `7a30992`) already landed a strictly better implementation of the same fix.

## What I learned from your version

Comparing my `manager.py` (423 lines, 3 public methods) against yours (395 lines, 7 public methods + 5 collaborating sub-components):

| | My PR #140 | PR #141 |
|---|---|---|
| Public methods on ExperienceManager | `record`, `retrieve`, `verify` (3) | `record`, `verify`, `retrieve`, `transfer`, `revalidate`, `supersede`, `get_conflicts` (7) |
| Architecture | Monolithic manager | Composition: `ExperienceManager` orchestrates `VerificationGate` + `EnvironmentChecker` + `ConflictResolver` + `ExperienceRetriever` + `RevalidationEngine` |
| Lifecycle covered | record → verify → retrieve | record → verify → retrieve → transfer → revalidate → supersede |
| Modules in `cognicore/experience/` | 2 new (`__init__.py`, `manager.py`) | 8 new — the 5 above plus `__init__.py`, `manager.py`, and proper separation |
| Scope of PR | 518 lines, 3 files | 8,563 lines, 61 files |

Three concrete things your design does better than mine, that I'm taking as lessons:

1. **Composition over monolith.** I stuffed `record` / `retrieve` / `verify` into a single class with private helpers. You split each concern into its own class with a result type (`VerificationGate` → `VerificationResult`, `EnvironmentChecker` → `CompatibilityResult`, `ConflictResolver` → `ConflictRecord`, `ExperienceRetriever` → `RetrievalResult`, `RevalidationEngine` → `RevalidationResult`). That makes each piece independently testable and reusable. My version was testable but not reusable.

2. **Lifecycle, not just CRUD.** My implementation handled `record / retrieve / verify` because that was all the chatgpt integration called. You added `transfer / revalidate / supersede / get_conflicts` — the full transfer-and-revalidation lifecycle that the experience schema was clearly designed for but no one had wired up. I solved the import error; you solved the missing feature.

3. **The bug was missing the whole subsystem, not just one class.** I treated this as "add the missing class" — minimum viable fix to make CI green. You treated it as "add the missing subsystem" — which is what the schema actually implied. Same root cause observation, very different ambition ceiling.

## Why I'm closing instead of resolving conflicts

The branch is in `dirty` state (add/add conflicts on both new files). I could resolve them and force-push, but the result would be my smaller implementation overwriting yours on those files — that's a downgrade, not an improvement. Closing is the honest move.

## The pre-existing CI failure is also yours to fix (if you want to)

After merge `7a30992`, CI still fails on `test (3.10)` but for a *new* reason — `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'requests'` in `tests/test_content_studio.py` (11 tests). That's from the same PR #141 (the AI Content Studio side of it). Not my place to fix it; flagging it because I noticed it while checking the post-merge CI status.

---

Thanks for landing the better version. Closing this PR without merge.

Refs: PR #141 (`7a30992`), my PR #140 (this one, closing).
